html:
Kowloon Walled City was a small walled enclave in Kowloon, Hong Kong, which grew into the most densely populated place in the world before it was demolished in 1993 and 1994.

It began as a Qing fort. When Britain leased the New Territories in 1898, China kept a claim to it, and neither government ruled it in practice for decades. After the Second World War squatters and refugees built over it.

By the 1980s about 33,000 people lived in a single block of some 350 buildings, joined by narrow passages where daylight hardly reached. There were factories, unlicensed dentists and doctors, and for years triad gangs, drugs and gambling. After the Joint Declaration, both governments agreed to clear it. It is now a park. Its image lives on in films, comics and video games.
sum: Kowloon Walled City was a small walled enclave in Kowloon, Hong Kong, which grew into the most densely populated place in the world before it was demolished in 1993 and 1994.
